svg.aria-label: How to tell a root, rhizome, tuber and bulb apart (schematic): a root has lengthwise wrinkles and lenticels on its surface, branch and fibrous roots lower down, and a cut surface showing bark, cambium ring and wood, often with radial lines and cracks (chrysanthemum heart); the lutou at the top of a ginseng main root is a piece of rhizome with bowl-shaped stem scars; root tubers (Dihuang, Heshouwu) are also roots. A rhizome has rings of nodes, with stem scars, buds or bud scars on top, fibrous roots or root scars on the underside and at the nodes, and leaf scars or remains of leaf bases at the nodes; the cut rhizome of Gancao (liquorice) has pith in the centre. A tuber (Tianma, gastrodia) has several rings of dots formed by dormant buds, a parrot's-beak bud or stem stump at the top, a round navel-like scar at the other end, and a horny, translucent cut surface. A bulb is made of fleshy scale leaves clasped together: in Chuanbei (songbei) the 2 outer scales, the big one tightly clasping the small one (moon held in the arms); Baihe (lily) uses single fleshy scale leaves with straight, parallel white vascular bundles. You cannot identify a herb from its root alone: identify the parts above ground while the plant is in flower or fruit, then dig
svg.title: Root, rhizome, tuber or bulb

g.text: How to tell a root, rhizome, tuber and bulb apart
(Schematic of crude herbs: look first for nodes, buds and stem scars on the surface, then at the cut surface;
for each herb, follow the description in its chapter)
① Root (e.g. Huangqi (astragalus), Gancao (liquorice), Jiegeng (balloon flower),
the surface; branch and fibrous roots
· Cut surface: bark, cambium ring and
② Rhizome (e.g. Huangjing (Solomon's seal), Yuzhu (fragrant Solomon's seal), Zhimu (anemarrhena),
· Rings of nodes all along; internode
· Stem scars, buds or bud scars on top
· Fibrous roots or root scars on the
· Leaf scars or remains of leaf bases
· Several rings of dots on the surface,
· At the top, a parrot's-beak bud (winter
tianma) or a stem stump (spring tianma)
· A round, navel-like scar at the other end
· Fakes lack this set of features
④ Bulb (e.g. Chuanbeimu (Sichuan fritillary), Zhebeimu (Zhejiang fritillary), Baihe (lily))
Baihe: a single fleshy scale leaf
· Made of fleshy scale leaves clasped
big one tightly clasping the small one
· Zhebei: large; single scale leaves or
· Baihe: single fleshy scale leaves are used
⚠️ You cannot identify a herb from its root alone: identify the parts above ground
while the plant is in flower or fruit, then dig up the underground part
Treat a piece of root on its own as "of unknown origin"
Corms also count as roots and rhizomes, but no herb in this part's chapters is a corm, so none is shown
